newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian support up for peace, guerrilla attacks.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian support up for peace, guerrilla attacks.

text.p: Palestinian support for peace moves with Israel has grown since a wave of violence between Jews and Arabs in the West Bank and Gaza Strip three months ago, a Palestinian research centre said on Tuesday.
But in the last 10 months, support for guerrilla attacks against Israel has also increased.

The Centre for Palestine Research and Studies said 79.3 percent of those questioned supported the peace process between Israel and the PLO with 15.8 percent expressing opposition and 4.8 percent saying they had no opinion.
It said 70 percent expressed support for peace moves in a similar poll three months ago.

The centre said 39.5 percent of those polled supported "armed attacks against Israeli targets" compared with 20 percent last March. Just over 48 percent said they opposed attacks and 12.1 percent had no opinion.
The centre questioned 1,307 adults throughout the West Bank and Gaza for the poll.

A wave of Palestinian suicide bombings killed 59 people in the Jewish state last February and March and were widely cited as factor in the electoral defeat of the left-leaning Labour government in May elections.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who ousted Labour, has conducted peace moves at a slower pace, opposing the exchange of land for peace with the Arabs.
His decision to open a second entrance to an archaeological tunnel near a Moslem shrine in Jerusalem last October sparked gun battles that killed 60 Palestinians and 15 Israeli troops.
The poll put unemployment in the West Bank and Gaza Strip at 31 percent.
